Definition: Water standing at its own level in a hollow of the ground. A terrain can have many.
A low place in the ground with higher ground all around it, which can hold water.
The lowest point on the edge of a hollow. Water rising above it spills over and runs away downhill.
The height of a lake's flat surface.
How far above the ground under the brush the water tools put the water. It is set in the Brush section.
One small square of the ground, as wide as the space between the terrain's height samples. A filled lake is made of cells that hold water or not.
A set of steps, in order, that solves a problem, such as filling a hollow with water.
A waiting list where the most important item always comes out first, such as the lowest cell when filling a lake.
An input chosen to check a program, with the result you expect from it.
